Senses.Explanation: Literally kudzu-and-wisteria creepers — vines that twist, cling and choke. In Chan it is the standing metaphor for WORDS that entangle: talk, verbiage, verbal complication, the case (公案) as a thicket of language. Yuanwu equates it outright with speech — (那裏如此葛藤)。(須是斬斷語言) 'why all this vine-tangle here? one must cut off words.' A teacher who explains too much is (打葛藤) 'spinning out vines'; the cases themselves are (葛藤公案) 'vine-tangle cases'; merely wordy Chan is disparaged as (葛藤禪) 'vine-Chan' (one pejorative label in a whole doxographic list of bad 'Chans'). The word carries a negative, self-deprecating cast — even a master opening a talk calls it (與諸人葛藤) 'getting tangled up in vines with you all.' It names the tangle of language, which the texts speak of cutting through (截斷／斬斷葛藤). The deployment range is wide: (截斷葛藤) ('cut off the vines') is spoken as a standalone dismissal in live exchanges — (師以拄杖畫一畫云)。(截斷葛藤) ('the master drew one stroke with his staff and said: cut off the vines'), (喝一喝)。(截斷葛藤) ('gave a shout: cut off the vines'); the tangle is a nest one sits or crashes into, (葛藤窠) — (坐在葛藤窠裡) ('sitting in the vine-nest'), (商量也依前撞入葛藤窠) ('discuss it and you crash into the vine-nest as before'); and the label reaches all the way up to the canon itself — (一大藏教閑葛藤)。(千七百則絆殺人) ('the whole great treasury of the teachings: idle vine-tangle; the seventeen hundred cases trip men to death'), and independently (一大藏教閑葛藤)。(盡大地人跳不出) ('idle vine-tangle the whole earth's people cannot jump clear of').
Senses.Note: Single corpus-wide metaphorical sense. The literal botanical 'kudzu vine' underlies it but in the Zen records the term is almost always the figurative 'verbal entanglement.' Counts (462-text allowlist grep): (葛藤) 2530 hits in 334 of the 462 texts; (打葛藤) 188 in 98; (葛藤窠) 144 in 81 (坐在葛藤窠裡 J10nA158 0004b05; 撞入葛藤窠 C078n1720 0669b19); (截斷葛藤) 80 in 60 (staff-stroke dismissals J25nB171 0519a07, 0535c08; 喝一喝 J26nB177 0038c28); (葛藤露布) 33 in 27; (葛藤禪) 21 in 18; (閑葛藤) 5 in 5 (一大藏教閑葛藤 J34nB299 0126a19 and X71n1420 0640a07).

Occurrences.Kwic: 那裏如此葛藤。須是斬斷語言。格外見諦。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (碧巖錄), Yuanwu's commentary glossing (葛藤) directly as (語言) (words): 'why such vine-tangle here? one must cut off words and see the truth beyond the letter.' The defining equation.

Occurrences.Kwic: 許多葛藤公案。具眼者。試說看。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanwu: 'so many vine-tangle cases — let the clear-eyed one try to explain.' The collocation (葛藤公案) (case-as-verbal-thicket).

Occurrences.Kwic: 道者禪葛藤禪。更有脫略機境不受差排者。喚作向上禪。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Extensive Record of Tianmu Zhongfeng (天目中峰廣錄): Zhongfeng Mingben lists proliferated labels for Chan, including 'entangling-vine Chan,' before criticizing the multiplication of names.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂。事不獲已。與諸人葛藤。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元): in Qingshan Puning's explicitly headed section, Qingshan Puning opens his hall address by saying that circumstances leave him no choice but to entangle vines with the listeners.
